title: Sections of filtered sheaf colimits over quasi-compact site objects
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ its category of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Call an object $W$ quasi-compact if every covering $\{V_a\to W\}_{a\in A}$ admits a covering refinement $\{T_b\to W\}_{b\in B}$ together with a map $\alpha:B\to A$ with finite image and factorizations $T_b\to V_{\alpha(b)}\to W$. Let $D$ be a small filtered category (nonempty, with a cocone on every finite diagram), let $G:D\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be a diagram and let $L=\varinjlim_DG$ in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every quasi-compact $W$, the canonical homomorphism $\varinjlim_dG_d(W)\to L(W)$ is injective. If $W$ has a cofinal system of finite covering families $\{W_a\to W\}_{a\in A}$ for which every pairwise fibre product $W_a\times_WW_b$ is quasi-compact, then this canonical homomorphism is an isomorphism. Here cofinal means that every covering of $W$ is refined by one of those families, and refinement means that each refining arrow factors through some original covering arrow.

proof.text: Put $P(V)=\varinjlim_dG_d(V)$ in abelian groups, with restrictions induced by the restrictions of the $G_d$; functoriality follows by checking the colimit coprojections. The abelian-sheaf colimit construction identifies $L$ with $P^\#$, compatibly with these coprojections. Sheafification of an abelian presheaf on underlying sets is set sheafification. Consequently the local-sections theorem applies to the underlying set map $\eta:P\to L$: every section of $L$ locally lifts to $P$, and equality of the images of two sections of $P(V)$ holds on a covering of $V$ already in $P$. Work in one universe containing the site, covering indices, diagram and group values; thus all the small-colimit and sheafification hypotheses of the cited statements hold.

proof.text: The forgetful functor from abelian groups to sets preserves the filtered colimit defining each $P(V)$. The elementwise filtered-set-colimit theorem therefore gives: every $p\in P(V)$ is represented by $t\in G_i(V)$, and if $t,t'\in G_i(V)$ have the same image in $P(V)$, some single arrow $a:i\to j$ satisfies $G(a)_V(t)=G(a)_V(t')$. The same applies to restrictions of these sections and to zero. We use these two conclusions below for the groups $P(V)$, not for $L(V)$ before its comparison has been proved injective.

source.place: Tag 0738, lemma-directed-colimits-sections, proof (2),(4), eventual equality in sectionwise filtered colimits

proof.text: For any quasi-compact object $V$, suppose $t\in G_i(V)$ maps to zero in $L(V)$. Step 1 supplies a covering $\{V_a\to V\}$ on which its class in $P$ is zero. Step 2 gives, for each $a$, an arrow $f_a:i\to j_a$ killing $t|_{V_a}$. By quasi-compactness choose a covering $\{T_b\to V\}$ factoring through the $V_{\alpha(b)}$ with $A_0=\alpha(B)$ finite. Apply filteredness to the finite diagram consisting of one labelled copy of $i$, one labelled copy of each $j_a$ for $a\in A_0$, and the arrows $f_a$. Its cocone gives $h:i\to k$ and $h_a:j_a\to k$ with $h=h_a f_a$. Naturality shows $G(h)_V(t)$ restricts to zero on every $T_b$. Sheaf separatedness for this covering gives $G(h)_V(t)=0$. If $A_0$ is empty, use $k=i$, $h=\mathrm{id}$ and the same separatedness for the empty covering. Finally any element of the kernel of $P(V)\to L(V)$ has a representative $t$ by step 2, so its eventual vanishing makes that element zero. This proves injectivity and, more precisely, eventual vanishing for a section at a specified stage.

Now impose the finite-cover hypothesis on $W$, and take $s\in L(W)$. By step 1 it lifts to sections of $P$ on some covering of $W$. Choose a covering $\{W_a\to W\}_{a\in A}$ from the specified cofinal system refining it. Restrict the chosen local lifts along the factorization maps, and use step 2 to represent them by $t_a\in G_{i_a}(W_a)$. The set $A$ is finite. A cocone in $D$ on the finite discrete diagram of its labelled indices gives $i$ and arrows $b_a:i_a\to i$. Replace $t_a$ by $G(b_a)t_a$. Thus all local lifts lie in $G_i$ and still have images $s|_{W_a}$ in $L$, by the cocone equations. If the cover is empty, choose any $i$, which exists because $D$ is nonempty; no local lift is required.

source.place: Tag 0738, lemma-directed-colimits-sections, proof (4), choosing finitely many local representatives

proof.text: For each $(a,b)\in A^2$, put $Z_{ab}=W_a\times_WW_b$ with its two projections. The difference of the restrictions of $t_a$ and $t_b$ is in $G_i(Z_{ab})$ and maps to zero in $L(Z_{ab})$, since both images restrict $s$ along the same composite to $W$. Each $Z_{ab}$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis. The eventual-vanishing assertion proved in step 3 gives $f_{ab}:i\to j_{ab}$ killing that difference. A cocone on the finite star diagram of all $f_{ab}$ gives a single $h:i\to k$ factoring through every $f_{ab}$. Hence the sections $G(h)t_a$ agree on every pairwise fibre product. The sheaf equalizer condition for $G_k$ glues them to $t\in G_k(W)$. Its image in $L(W)$ restricts to $s|_{W_a}$ for all $a$, so separatedness of $L$ makes that image $s$. For an empty cover take $k=i$ and use the equalizer condition on the empty family, which gives the unique section and the same equality. This proves surjectivity. The object $W$ is itself quasi-compact: a covering $\{V_c\to W\}_{c\in C}$ is refined by a family $\{W_a\to W\}_{a\in A}$ of the system, and choosing for each $a$ one $c=\alpha(a)$ with $W_a\to W$ factoring through $V_c$ gives $\alpha:A\to C$ with finite image since $A$ is finite. Hence step 3 applies to $V=W$; together with it, the comparison is a bijective homomorphism. Its inverse preserves addition because, for images $x,y$, the unique preimage of $x+y$ is the sum of their unique preimages; thus it is an isomorphism of abelian groups.
